title: Optimize Recurring High-Cost ETL Query
problem_description: A recurring query (hash: 0df70a5ed58208625f0b20ab13e57c208ce416b237b67fbc55b12684af398442), executed by vinay.chaudhari@onixnet.com, consistently processes ~9.5 TB of data, resulting in significant cost. The query suffers from severe performance issues, including spilling over 2 TB of shuffle data to disk and experiencing slot contention, leading to execution times exceeding one hour.
recommendation: The query must be rewritten to avoid the massive data shuffle. Investigate the JOIN and GROUP BY clauses. Potential solutions include using clustering on the source table (trawoutput_org) on the join keys, pre-aggregating data in a staging table, or using approximate aggregation functions if business requirements permit. The goal is to reduce the data volume before the shuffle stage.

financial_impact.assumptions: Assumes the query is executed daily (365 days/year). Savings are based on optimizing the query to reduce bytes billed by at least 90%.

title: Refactor Daily CTAS jobs to use Partitioning
problem_description: The user vinay.chaudhari@onixnet.com is creating daily tables using CREATE_TABLE_AS_SELECT (e.g., Impala_Eagle_Output_20250903). This is an anti-pattern that leads to massive data duplication, increased storage costs, and inefficient, full-table-scan queries.
recommendation: Cease the creation of date-sharded tables. Create a single, permanent table (e.g., 'trawoutput_partitioned') partitioned by a DATE or TIMESTAMP column. Refactor the daily ETL job to use an INSERT or MERGE statement to append or update data in the correct partition of this new table. This will drastically reduce the data processed for each run and eliminate redundant storage.

financial_impact.estimated_cost_per_query: Reduced proportionally to the amount of data scanned. Instead of 9.5 TB, it would scan only the daily delta.
financial_impact.assumptions: Savings depend on the size of the daily delta vs. the full table size. Annual savings include both reduced query costs and the elimination of storing ~9.5 TB of redundant data every day.

title: Investigate Slot Contention
problem_description: Multiple queries, especially the large ETL jobs, are reporting 'slot_contention'. This indicates that the number of available slots is insufficient for the workload, causing queries to queue and run slower, which increases total slot-hour consumption under a flat-rate model.
recommendation: While the primary solution is to optimize the inefficient queries (REC-001, REC-002) which are hogging resources, a secondary analysis of slot utilization is recommended. Review the BigQuery Admin project's slot usage charts. If contention persists after optimization, consider purchasing additional slots or implementing a reservation system to isolate batch workloads from interactive queries.

financial_impact.assumptions: Improving slot efficiency reduces the need to purchase more slots and improves query performance for all users.
